statement: The history of a document is the chain of its head. A revision index is returned only when its last entry is the head's (revision and digest) and each entry above the lowest names, as its parent, the digest of the entry below it; otherwise it is rebuilt from the head's records, replacing only an entry still as the walk compared it, and nothing below the retention floor; an entry that cannot be shown to be on the chain (below a record the walk could not read) is not returned. The write path never replaces a listed revision number that has another digest; the digests a rebuild replaces are left to reclamation, which never deletes a digest the history lists, and the rebuild is logged once with the key and each revision's dropped and kept digest.

control:HistoryForkTest#a late settle of the old branch does not put its entry back under the new one
control:HistoryForkTest#a publication leaves a number listed with another digest as it is
control:HistoryForkTest#the repair says what it unlisted, once
control:HistoryForkTest#an index that agrees with the head is returned without reading a record
control:HistoryForkTest#an entry written without a parent is rewritten with it by a read
control:HistoryForkTest#a record missing below the head hides what cannot be shown to be on the chain
control:HistoryForkTest#a head restored to a replaced digest is listed again and not reclaimed
control:HistoryForkTest#a republication of a number between the walk and the write is not overwritten
control:HistoryForkTest#a repair that a reclamation overtakes lists nothing below its floor
control:VerifyIndexTest#an index one revision behind the head is a publication settling, two behind differs
control:VerifyIndexTest#an index with another digest at the head's revision, or none at all, differs
control:VerifyIndexTest#a verification between a head write and its index write finds a note, not a finding
